auditor_value: a₂ = −7a₁ (block 2 accelerates 7 times as much as block 1, in the opposite direction); intermediate a₃ = −a₁, a₄ = −3a₁

findings.quote: Treating the chain of movable pulleys as a single ordinary pulley and taking a₂ = a₁ instead of a₂ = 7a₁.
findings.note: Vague, and written without the sign convention the solution itself uses: with all positions measured downward the final answer is a₂ = −7a₁, and a single fixed pulley would give a₂ = −a₁, not a₂ = a₁. The entry names no actual step a student gets wrong.
findings.fix: Writing only the top string's constraint (x₁ + x₃ = constant) and stopping there, which gives |a₂| = |a₁|; each movable pulley below adds its own constraint, and combining all three gives a₂ = −7a₁.

notes: Independently, with x measured downward from the line through P₁: S₁ gives a₁ + a₃ = 0; S₂ gives a₁ + a₄ − 2a₃ = 0; S₃ gives a₁ + a₂ − 2a₄ = 0; hence a₃ = −a₁, a₄ = −3a₁, a₂ = −7a₁. Every printed equation follows from the one above it. The why_this_step on the last step is informal ('multiplies the effect') but not false.
